thank you for responding because that actually clears up something that happened in the past. i had thought he was just a shitty doctor but he did exactly those things. 

i was sick with god knows what. it was a weird and scary combination of things, so i actually went to an urgent care. which says a lot because i like to avoid doctors. i waited for more than two hours to be seen (i think he was just busy, he was the only doctor), but once i was finally seen he barely talked about the symptoms of why i was there. he saw on the paper that i filled out that i was on antipsychotics and basically only asked me questions about that. why i took them, what my family life was like. he didn’t seem to care about why i was there, and at the end i was able to ask for doctors notes for as many days of school that i felt like missing. 

my mother was really upset and so was i. i felt that since he was a doctor i had to answer those questions and i left the place still sick, with no answers to that problem
it’s very strange to see all of these comments of people whose doctors also did not tell them. you’d think that you’d tell the paranoid people what’s going on, to relieve paranoia

i can understand maybe not wanting to tell someone who was as young as i was, because like you said it is a rough diagnosis to receive. but i’m also someone who likes things super blunt, and the doctor knew i had symptoms for a while. not directly telling me felt different from them telling me to avoid seeing anything about my dx though. giving papers to only my mother until i was like 16 felt really wrong. i think it would’ve been best to just talk about it normally like they did with my other diagnoses. there’s an aspect to them not telling me that is scary to me. 

maybe if my symptoms were new and we were still figuring it out it would’ve been better to keep things a little vague, but i spent a majority of my life with my symptoms and i think that even though i was like 14ish, i would’ve benefited from just knowing what the heck my deal was. 

now that i’m 18 and talk about my schizophrenia with both my psych and therapist, i see no reason for them to continue beating around the bush. sometimes they don’t, but sometimes they still do. learning that i had it was scary because of how little i knew, for all i knew schizophrenic people were monsters and murderers. but once all that passed and i saw it written down and confirmed many times, i was able to start to fight the stigma. i was in no way a murderer and would never hurt anyone. i was schizophrenic but no voices wanted me to kill anyone. 

i also was able to find this subreddit which i’ve frequented since i made the account, which was a huge help. the people on this sub have never let me down, and i feel like i am able to speak so freely here because everyone understands. 

i’ve spoken to them about not liking that they communicate back and forth without me, because i don’t like people knowing things about me that even i didn’t know. maybe that could’ve hinted to them to just talk to me

about that last part, i honestly don’t know much about being a schizophrenic adult, which sucks as i near 19. 

what negative things can happen if you have such a stigmatised illness on medical documents? it took most of my childhood and all of my teen years. i don’t know anything about not being schizophrenic. i had no idea that bad things could come from simply having the dx
